notes.name: Wikipedia · Inge Morath
notes.q: Morath's first encounter with avant-garde art was the Entartete Kunst (Degenerate Art) exhibition organized by the Nazi Party in 1937, which sought to inflame public opinion against modern art.

src.name: Wikipedia · Inge Morath
src.q: In 1936, the family moved to  Berlin where Morath's father directed the Research Institute for Plywood and Wood Products (German: Leitung des Forschungsinstituts für Sperrholz und andere Holzerzeugnisse).

src.name: Wikipedia · Inge Morath
src.q: Morath was briefly married to the British journalist Lionel Birch and relocated to London in 1951.

notes.q: The book Last Journey (2002), and Strasseger's film Grenz Räume (Border Space, 2002), document Morath's visits to her homeland during the final years of her life.
